concerns.text: The plan explicitly relies on 'synthetic generation of environmental covariates' (proxy data) because the verified MODIS dataset is spatially insufficient. A model trained on synthetic temperature/NDVI surfaces cannot predict real-world avian migration patterns. The research question (predicting actual migration) becomes unanswerable by this method, as the input features do not represent the physical reality driving the biological phenomenon. This is an idea-root flaw.

The plan proposes using the Diebold-Mariano test to compare model performance (RMSE) on a dataset where the predictors (Temp/NDVI) are synthetic. While the test is statistically valid for comparing two models, the conclusion that 'the combined model significantly outperforms the baseline' is scientifically meaningless if the underlying data is simulated. The test validates the *code's* ability to detect differences in synthetic noise, not the *science* of migration drivers.

The plan correctly identifies the study as 'associational' but fails to address the confound of 'observer effort' in the synthetic data generation. If the synthetic environmental data is generated independently of the eBird observation density (which is highly spatially biased), the model may learn spurious correlations between the synthetic grid values and the biased observation counts, rather than true biological signals. The plan lacks a design to control for this specific confound in the proxy data.
